# SDCoreJS Artifact Lifecycle

This reference defines ownership, metadata, runtime propagation, Git closure,
and redaction rules for `.sdcorejs/**` artifacts. Read it before any workflow
writes, verifies, stages, commits, or pushes those artifacts.

`_refs/shared/artifact-lifecycle.mjs` provides a deterministic, read-only
discovery and classification helper. It never stages or commits files.

Blueprints use `.sdcorejs/blueprints/<kebab>.json` and the shared-owned
`project-blueprint` kind; read-only discovery cannot grant write ownership.
Product snapshots, assets and delivery receipts use the registry ticket root and
`ticket-snapshot`, `ticket-asset`, `ticket-delivery` kinds. Validate canonical
identity paths, JSON metadata, matching `change_ref` and exact filename/byte
hashes. Metadata cannot claim a ticket kind outside that root. Asset promotion
resolves a stored same-change snapshot, matching path/hash/size and, for binary
images, a privacy review bound to those bytes. Runtime bucket assertions alone
cannot promote an image. Reference images never become real UI test evidence.
Ticket files or parent paths that are symlinks fail closed. Preserve immutable
snapshots across refreshes; raw downloads and failed unreviewed captures remain
local diagnostics. See `../product/ticket-intake.md` for the writer protocol.
Delivery plans and receipts pass `readTicketDelivery` and resolve their exact
stored complete source snapshot. Identity, revision, source hash, owner and
change must match; an absent source or cross-ticket receipt remains unknown.
Closure follows validated snapshot attachments and delivery source references,
including already committed files. Available attachments

# Documentation Layout Contract

Use this reference only when a workflow creates, discovers, reads, updates, migrates,
aggregates, exports, validates, or closes documentation below
`.sdcorejs/documentation/`. It is not bootstrap context for unrelated work.

Document identity and containment stay in this layout. Audience and outline are
selected through `../documentation/documentation-profile.md`, with
`documentation_profile_version`, `documentation_scope` and
`documentation_audience` metadata. Scope may be module, entity, feature, task,
role, state or journey without adding competing category roots. Existing manual
prose is preserved by the safe update planner. Aggregate composition validates
then removes per-source managed-block delimiters so generated projections do not
inherit conflicting editing ownership; malformed markers block the build.
Approved requirement coverage retains stable AC identities from verified current
specs. A `gap` or `conflict` propagates with null counts through module and
cross-repository aggregates, displayed as not assessed; it is never summed as
zero successful coverage. Observed-behavior guides remain usable with this gap
visible. See the profile reference for trusted-host receipt validation.
Legacy counts without explicit `selected` status remain unassessed. Selected
counts must be nonnegative integers whose met/partial/missing sum equals total;
null, malformed or inconsistent values remain a gap. Successful aggregation
preserves the selected status instead of dropping its authority marker.
